title: Tenant upgrade SLA phasing and rollout safety net
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: A subset of enterprise customers (VPC/on-prem and dedicated private tenants) need a clear, low-risk upgrade lane that preserves SLA commitments and provides automatic safety nets. Recent pilot upgrades surfaced three failure modes: kernel incompatibility on legacy quantized models, CIDR/network drift during hot-reconfig, and insufficient telemetry to detect token-level regressions quickly.

Goal: Deliver a phased SLA-aware upgrade playbook and programmatic safety net that: 1) defines upgrade phasing (canary -> staggered -> full), 2) maps SLO windows and customer-facing SLA guarantees per phase, 3) implements automatic fallback and readable runbooks, and 4) exposes console signals for rollout health (failure budget, latency delta, token-quality regressions).

Success metrics: 1) 0 P0 customer incidents attributable to upgrades for first 30 days post-upgrade for canary tenants; 2) rollback decision latency < 10 minutes when health signals cross thresholds; 3) telemetry coverage >= 95% for token-level quality checks on rollout cohorts; 4) documented runbook and customer comms template published before first tranche.

Constraints and trade-offs: - Conservative phasing reduces upgrade velocity but minimizes customer risk. - Full offline upgrades (longer maintenance windows) reduce runtime complexity but increase churn for customers; we will prioritize in-place upgrades with transparent maintenance windows where customers opt-in. - Some legacy customers require kernel pinning; cannot force quantization changes during rollout.

Outcomes / Deliverables: - Upgrade phasing spec (canary criteria, cohort sizing, stagger cadence). - Console rollout dashboard with live failure budget and quality delta widgets. - Automated safety net: if latency or quality threshold breached, route new traffic to previous model variant and trigger alerting runbook. - Customer comms templates and consent flow for staggered upgrades. - Post-upgrade verification checklist and telemetry dashboards.

Acceptance criteria: - Spec approved by Eng and Security. - Console dashboard QA complete with synthetic traffic and demo. - Runbook tested in staging with simulated rollback (2 simulated failures). - Customer communication templates reviewed by Legal.

Stakeholders: Product: Maya Chen (owner), Eng: Owen Patel (assignee), Security: Lina García, SRE: Priyanka Rao, Solutions Eng: Ben Thompson, Legal/Comms: Rachel Li.
